# tsk

> tsk is a terminal task board for you and your agents: one shared queue, a TUI for you, a CLI for them.

On macOS/Linux, install with `curl -fsSL https://gettsk.sh/install.sh | sh` or `brew install smarzban/tap/tsk`. On Windows 10/11 ARM64 or x86-64, run `irm https://www.gettsk.sh/install.ps1 | iex` in a PowerShell window (Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7); it selects the native architecture. Download the script first to use `-NoPathUpdate`, which leaves user PATH unchanged. Windows package-manager submissions and signing are not included yet.
If Herdr is on PATH, the installer asks to run `tsk setup herdr` on an interactive terminal; when agent skill roots are detected it also asks once to install the tsk skill. The install ends with a single `Done.` line pointing at the board (plus the Herdr board shortcut after an accepted Herdr setup) and one row per skipped ask (`tsk setup herdr`, `tsk setup`); a custom `TSK_INSTALL_DIR` skips the asks and says so. Homebrew prints the Herdr setup command as a caveat.
Herdr's board shortcut opens or focuses one board per workspace across its tabs, preserving its view and edits. Other workspaces stay untouched; boards share the same task store.
Details: https://gettsk.sh/docs/install.md
Inside Git, the repo root is the default project. Outside Git, tsk opens and captures on the desk while keeping the current directory available as a project. In `!p name`, `tsk add -p name`, and JSON plans, a bare project name must uniquely match a known project; a new project destination requires an existing absolute directory (`/…` or `~/…` on macOS/Linux, `C:\…` or `~\…` on Windows).
New tasks start with status `open` in the board's inbox, below picked `ready` tasks. Use the ready and open board commands to move them between groups, and `tsk list --open` or `--ready` to filter. The board checks GitHub releases at most daily and shows a dim `vX.Y.Z available, run tsk update` on the status row; set `TSK_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` to disable. Run `tsk update` to run the official installer for an installer-managed copy; on Windows a detached helper waits for the running executable to exit before replacing it. Existing Herdr registration and outdated installed agent skills are refreshed; when no agent skill is installed, an interactive update can offer the first-install skill setup. Homebrew copies print `brew update && brew upgrade tsk` instead.
Store format v6 adds optional task assignees, explicit base branches, and dispatch records, including a cleaned marker retained after worktree removal. A v5 store migrates on first save and keeps a `tsk.json.v5` backup; v5 batch undo and earlier migrations still run in order.
Agent launch profiles live in `<state dir>/config.toml` (tsk settings) beside `tsk.json`; unknown top-level keys are ignored; the first full board open seeds commented examples when the file is missing, while quick capture and CLI commands do not. `[agent.<name>]` tables define a required argv `command`, an optional prompt template, and optional string environment values. `{number}`, `{title}`, `{notes}`, `{steps}`, `{worktree}`, `{branch}`, and `{base}` work in command and prompt templates; the rendered profile or default prompt is always appended as the command's last argument. The default prompt names the task, worktree, branch, and base; tells the agent to read `tsk guide`, `tsk list <n> --json` (the notes are the brief), and the repo's AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md; to work only on the task branch and run the project's checks; to push and open a pull request into the base and never merge it; then to set the task to review with one line on what to look at, or blocked with its question. The seeded starter file quotes that default and has commented examples for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Grok, and any other terminal agent. `{base}` is the short base branch name (for example `dispatch` for `origin/dispatch`), so prompts can say "open the PR into {base}". Tasks can be assigned only to exact profile names: use `!a name`, the assignee picker, task-page Assignee, palette **set assignee**, or `tsk add/edit --assignee`; clear with bare `!a` or `--unassign`. `tsk list --assignee name` filters assigned work. Task and expanded-capture edits move Title → Notes → steps → + step → Assignee → Base → Thread → Scope.
Explicit dispatch bases use `!b branch`, `tsk add/edit --base <branch>`, task-page Base, the clickable `⎇` footer, or palette **set base**. The branch picker offers the repository default first, then deduplicated local and origin branches; the picker opens at once on the branches already on disk and, unless origin was fetched in the last 60 seconds, shows a disabled `refreshing…` row while a bounded background fetch updates the list in place, keeping the selection (`offline, showing cached branches` if the fetch fails); typing filters it. Reopening reuses the project fetch already in flight, never adding another concurrent fetch. Palette base changes apply to marked tasks as one save and one undo. Choose default or use `--clear-base` to clear a task override. Bases must be existing branches in the task repository, not tags or commits; unknown branches refuse with `unknown-base`. There is no dedicated base shortcut and dispatch never prompts for one.
`N` tasks on the desk are human-only notices: four starter tasks on a first open, one `What's new in tsk` task after an upgrade. `tsk list` never shows them.
Peek footers are ordered `@assignee · ⎇ <base> · #thread · project`, omitting unset parts and hiding a default base. The task-page footer always shows a base: for example `⎇ main (default)` when unset, resolved from a cache without blocking rendering, with `⎇ default` as fallback. A task with a live dispatch that is still started uses `◉` instead of the ordinary started glyph `●`; other human statuses and cleaned dispatches keep their normal glyph. Dispatch on an unassigned task opens the assignee picker, saves the choice, then dispatches. Board dispatch asks for confirmation before relaunching an existing record; the palette offers **dispatch again**.
A first dispatch uses a one-off `tsk dispatch --base` override, then the explicit task base, otherwise the task repository's remote default (`origin/HEAD`). The board or CLI checkout never supplies the default. It fetches the base's remote first (bounded, best effort), using a local branch's remote upstream when present and reporting offline fallback to the local ref. Direct `tsk list T<n> --json` includes an optional full `dispatch` record after `thread`; `dispatch.base` is the display ref, `dispatch.base_ref` its fully qualified namespace used verbatim at cleanup, and `dispatch.base_commit` its starting commit SHA (legacy records may omit them). Filtered listings omit the dispatch record. Dispatch records the actual ref and commit; task pages show `from <ref> @ <short sha>` and cleanup cards show `Merged into <ref> ✓` or `Not merged into <ref>`. Cleanup fetches before checking ancestry against the recorded base, so a GitHub merge counts without a local pull. Dispatch, the branch picker and cleanup share a 60-second fetch window (successful fetches only, recorded in `fetch-stamps.json` for CLI runs): a remote fetched that recently is not fetched again. Every such fetch also refreshes the remote's default (`origin/HEAD`). The board's cleanup card opens with `checking…` until a background fetch fills merged status; `y` before then is queued (the card says so) and finishes when the check lands, keeping the branch if the check does not finish within its bound. Bulk `ctrl+d` on a marked set with live dispatches opens one card with a row per dispatch (merged status and what `y` will do); `y` cleans every clean worktree and completes the whole set in one save and one undo entry, `n` completes without cleanup, `Esc` keeps the marks. If fetch fails, the card and CLI human/JSON output warn that ancestry used cached refs. A missing or pruned base keeps the branch but does not block clean worktree removal. Kept branches report the actual reason (failed ancestry, checked out elsewhere, or changed during cleanup). Cleanup worktree listings, status and ancestry use a separate 10-second deadline: preflight timeouts refuse before removal, and a final branch-recheck timeout retains the branch with a reason. Dirty worktrees refuse; merged branches are removed, unmerged branches kept, and a cleaned dispatch record retained. Squash merges do not establish ancestry: the branch stays with an explanation such as "not merged into origin/main; squash-merged? delete by hand".
Multi-select marks a session-only set for status, archive, delete, assignee, and base changes. Leaving the mode, running an action, or changing the lens clears marks. Task details, editing, and dispatch remain cursor-only. At 110 usable columns or wider, clicking a task opens or updates its details beside the board with board focus. Double-click opens it full screen. Narrow panes use click-to-peek.
On Projects Overview, clicking or moving the index selection opens the cursored project's preview beside the index at Split, then a live narrow project board at Rail, never a full-screen task. The right board names the selected project in its top row and owns its own selection and actions. Expanding quick-add there keeps the draft title in that header while Notes is active; Esc returns to the index.

Press `/` on any board tab to filter the rows it shows. Projects Overview matches project names and paths; task boards match every whitespace-separated query term against title, notes, steps, thread, assignee, and `T` number. `Enter` pins the query and returns input to board keys, while `Esc` clears the input or a pinned query first. The done drawer is searched only while open, and changing tab, project, or Projects view clears search. In the wide Projects preview, `/` searches the right board when it has focus.

The quit shortcut exits from non-editor board surfaces, including task pages, Help, pickers, and the wide project preview. Text entry keeps its editing behavior; save recovery must be resolved first. Unsaved drafts block quitting, including drafts parked outside the focused project preview. Quit attempts preserve the pending save's failure message. Escape dismisses editors and overlays first, then collapses either wide split to its full-width board or projects index. Task drafts stay parked; unsaved work in a project preview prevents closing it. Escape then quits without confirmation at the full-board root on any tab, never switching tabs first. A narrow resize that hides the right column also exposes that root; parked drafts still block quitting. The browser demo releases keyboard focus at root instead of exiting. See the Keys guide for shortcuts.

## For agents

- `tsk guide` prints the workflow; `tsk setup` detects agents and can install the skill; `tsk setup <agent>` targets one agent
- The skill covers rules of engagement, board language, the exit contract, and workflows, and points at `tsk help <command>` for syntax; its `Refine a task` section shapes a rough task into a brief on the board (propose, then write)
- `tsk list T<n>` returns the complete task, including notes, steps, assignee, base, thread, and dispatch, in human-readable or JSON form
- `tsk dispatch T<n>` launches assigned project work in Herdr (macOS and Linux only; Windows refuses with `unsupported-platform`); a first launch creates branch `tsk/t<n>-<slug>` (lowercased title with non-letter/digit runs as `-`, cut at a word boundary within 30 characters, none for a symbols-only title, `-2`, `-3` appended when the branch, worktree, or checkout directory is taken), worktree `tsk-t<n>-<slug>` (Herdr keeps only ASCII letters and digits in the directory name), and Herdr workspace label `T<n>` plus the title up to the same cut (`…` when cut); `--base <branch>` overrides a first launch; `--again` always keeps the recorded base, ignoring overrides and later task-base changes. It reuses a live dispatch or recreates a cleaned worktree, reopening a retained branch or recreating a removed branch from its original `base_commit` (legacy fallback: recorded base ref); the launched agent is named `t<n>-<assignee>` in Herdr when detected
- `tsk clean T<n> [--json]` removes only the recorded non-root project worktree and matching Herdr workspace; `tsk status T<n> done --clean` persists done before trying cleanup
- Guide: https://gettsk.sh/docs/agents.md
- CLI: https://gettsk.sh/docs/cli.md
- `tsk help [<command>]` prints the CLI or one command's syntax reference.
- `tsk --version` (or `tsk -V`) prints the installed version.

Storage, backups, and release-check settings: https://gettsk.sh/docs/storage.md
- Full docs: https://gettsk.sh/llms-full.txt
